## Summary

`scripts/mutation_gate.py` isolates the **source tree** (`git archive` into a temp dir)
but not **runtime effects**. On 2026-08-26 a mutation removed a guard from a shell
script that performs real deletion, a test exec'd that script with an empty path
variable, and the glob expanded to `rm -rf /*` — destroying `/opt/homebrew` and every
Homebrew-installed app in `/Applications` on a contributor workstation. Only a
60-second subprocess timeout stopped it; `/Users` was still ahead of it in the target
list.

## Which subprocess actually matters

`execute_shard()` spawns **four** subprocesses via `_run()`:

| Line | Subprocess | Executes shard test code? |
|---|---|---|
| 579 | baseline `pytest` | **Yes** — unmutated |
| 583 | `mutmut run --max-children 1` | **Yes — this is the causal path** |
| 595 | `mutmut results --all true` | No — reporting only |
| 612 | `mutmut show <mutant>` | No — reporting only |

The incident occurred under **`mutmut run`**, which executes the *mutated* code against
the suite. Sandboxing only the baseline `pytest` would leave the causal path exposed
and reproduce the incident exactly. Both test-executing subprocesses are in scope; the
two reporting subprocesses are not, because they execute no shard code.

`execute_shard()` has exactly two callers, both in `mutation_gate.py` (lines 697, 698
— the `base` and `head` runs), so the change surface is contained.

## Why source-tree isolation was never going to help

Researched across cargo-mutants, mutmut, StrykerJS, PIT and mull: **every one isolates
the source tree; none isolates runtime effects.** A copied tree does nothing when the
mutated code calls `rm -rf /` — the syscall still lands. cargo-mutants documents this
explicitly (https://mutants.rs/cautions.html): *"it might modify existing deletion
paths in your code… could potentially delete unintended directories… Run in an
isolated environment (container, CI, or VM)."* No mutation tool in any language ships
OS-level sandboxing; it is the caller's job.

## Why guards inside the script cannot substitute

The harness string-substitutes the artifact under test, so **any guard expressed in
that artifact can be deleted by a mutation** — including `${dir:?}`. Only a layer
outside the mutated artifact is load-bearing. Note `set -euo pipefail` would NOT have
fired: `set -u` triggers on *unset*, not set-but-empty, and the variable was `""`.

## Platform scope

POSIX only. `pyproject.toml:37-38` classifies the project `Operating System :: POSIX`
and `Operating System :: MacOS :: MacOS X`, and the CI matrix
(`_build-and-test.yml:311`) is `[ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]`. Windows is out of
scope because it is not a supported platform, not because it is unhandled.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both shard-test-executing subprocesses in `execute_shard()` — the baseline
      `pytest` (line 579) **and** the `mutmut run` mutant test-run (line 583) — are
      wrapped in an OS-enforced sandbox denying filesystem writes outside an explicit
      allow-list (scratch tree, pytest basetemp, the venv, `/dev/null`). Verified by
      `pytest tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py`.
- [ ] The enforcement test trips the deny under **`mutmut run`** specifically, not only
      under the baseline `pytest`, since `mutmut run` is the path the incident took.
- [ ] The sandbox demonstrably DENIES: a probe writing outside the allow-list exits
      non-zero and the file is absent afterward; the same probe inside the allow-list
      succeeds. Asserting wrapper argv alone does not satisfy this — the test observes
      enforcement, not construction.
- [ ] macOS uses Seatbelt `sandbox-exec` with a generated profile. Verified on a macOS
      host by `pytest tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py`.
- [ ] Linux uses `bwrap` (bubblewrap) when present, else `unshare --map-root-user
      --mount`; the chosen mechanism is probed at runtime, not assumed. Verified by a
      test that asserts the probe selects the available mechanism and reports which.
- [ ] With no sandbox mechanism available the run ABORTS non-zero with a message naming
      the opt-out env var. Verified by a test stubbing both mechanisms absent.
- [ ] The opt-out env var waives the sandbox and logs at WARNING when used; a silent
      unsandboxed fallback is rejected. Verified by asserting the WARNING record.
- [ ] Enforcement is an OS facility invoked in-process, never a CI-provider feature, and
      works from a developer laptop with no CI involved (`project.portability`).
- [ ] `HOME` is set to a non-existent path for both sandboxed subprocesses so adjacent
      home-directory writes fail loudly. Verified by asserting the child's `HOME`.
- [ ] A lint gate flags a test that `subprocess`-execs a shell script containing an
      unguarded destructive deletion, and passes when routed through an injectable seam
      such as `"${RM_CMD:-rm}"`. Verified by
      `python scripts/check_destructive_test_exec.py`.
- [ ] That gate runs in `make lint`, consistent with `check_raw_git_writes.py` and
      `check_wall_clock_asserts.py`. Verified by `make lint`.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py` — enforcement under both the baseline
  and `mutmut run`, mechanism probing, fail-closed abort, opt-out WARNING, and `HOME`.
- `pytest tests/scripts/test_check_destructive_test_exec.py` — the lint gate flags an
  unguarded destructive `subprocess`-exec and passes a seamed one.
- `pytest tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py` — the existing harness suite still passes
  (it monkeypatches `execute_shard` at lines 489, 540, 948).
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and
  `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` — all green.

## Definition of Done

- Every acceptance criterion above is checked, each by the command it names.
- The sandbox logic lands in its own module: `mutation_gate.py` is **762 LOC against
  the 800 hard cap**, so it cannot absorb this inline.
- Operator note documents the opt-out env var and the risk of using it.

## Notes

Filed from the 2026-08-26 incident. Two other leaks found the same day —
gate-snapshot accumulation (`a37c-d55c-72c3-439b`) and orphaned CPU load generators
(`f3d9-ecd8-df72-4fa1`) — are unrelated in cause and tracked separately.

The `mutmut run` scoping above was caught by this ticket's own plan review (finding
G6): the prior revision said "its pytest subprocess", which would have sandboxed the
baseline and left the causal path open.
